notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35018434/636b2276207aa616c32d834898cc7adc193ef286.png[/img]

The moment you’ve all been waiting for is here—it’s finally spring! Wait...that wasn’t the big news… Oh, right! Spring has finally arrived in [i]Tools Up[/i]! and the crew is back with the first-ever DLC, [i]Tools Up! Garden Party[/i]! Gather your friends for local co-op or play it yourself, but hop to it because these gardens need your help!

[h2]Watch the Tools Up! Garden Party Trailer[/h2]

[previewyoutube=02y8kZw7d6E;full][/previewyoutube]

[i]Tools Up! Garden Party[/i] features tons of new mechanics, tools, and exciting levels waiting to be discovered through three separate seasonal episodes. [i]Episode 1: The Tree House[/i] is available to play now while Episodes 2 and 3 will be available soon! Each episode will also feature a challenging opponent. In the first episode, keep a look out for a trickster raccoon—you’ll have to beat more than just the clock now! 

[h2]Check out the Release Roadmap[/h2]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35018434/3f78a746aa1127912eff5b7cc1c06c507411bd03.jpg[/img]

All [i]Garden Party[/i] episodes can be purchased together in the Season Pass for $14.99, or separately for $5.99. However, please note that to play Episodes 2 and 3 you must also have completed the previous episodes. Get your garden party started today!

https://store.steampowered.com/app/1415430/Tools_Up_Garden_Party__Episode_1_The_Tree_House/

https://store.steampowered.com/app/1408620/Tools_Up_Garden_Party__Season_Pass/

To make this occasion even more special, [i]Tools Up![/i] is on sale! If you haven’t already, [b]you can get the game 75% off when you get it before April 28[/b].

https://store.steampowered.com/app/1004490/Tools_Up/

[h2]The Tools Up! Garden Party Story[/h2]

The Tools Up! Co. crew were coming back from another successful renovation, when suddenly something fell on the road in front of them! They got out of the car and saw an enormous tree house surrounded by broken branches. It was practically falling apart before their eyes—this was going to take some work! It’s a good thing Tools Up! Co. was in the right place at the right time. Only they have the skills to restore order to this place!

[h2]What’s waiting for you in Episode 1?[/h2]

We don’t want to spoil all the surprises, but here’s a sneak peek at some of the features waiting for you in the tree house.

Growing plants need lots of care and watering. One of the fastest ways to get the job done is to use a garden hose, but will you be able to control its attempts to escape? It’s best to do this job with a friend to help you regulate the water’s flow, but if you go it alone you’d better hold on tight—thar she blows!

[img]https://i.imgur.com/f8USGhU.gif[/img]

A few artistic statues perfectly complement the look of any garden. Find your inner Michelangelo and make some statues yourself! If this sounds like the thing for you, then you’ll be pleased to find out that statues won’t be the only decorative items you'll be able to make in the game. Just be sure to place all your decorations according to the blueprint!

Something else that’s new in [i]Tools Up! Garden Party[/i] is that now, some tasks can be completed in more than one way. Anything goes when you’re in the wilderness of the great outdoors! Do you think you’ll be able to discover all the different methods?

On top of all your gardening duties, you’ll have to solve the mystery of the tree house before you can call the job done. Work your way through all three episodes and find out what’s been going on up there!

See you in the gardens, Renovators!

notes.title: How tags work on Steam
notes.content:
[b]Dear Players,[/b]
We are impressed by the amount of support we get from you lately! Thank you!

One of the insights we hear a lot and which seems particularly accurate is that some players might have been misled by the [i]Multiplayer[/i] tag on Steam into believing that Tools Up! is an online co-op game.

We have no doubt that it could be the case here. [i]Multiplayer[/i] is often associated with playing online (it's an understandable mental shortcut), even though it can also be local only, especially in the case of couch co-op games.

Now, the way tags work on Steam is that we can't toggle the Local Co-op tag without toggling the Multiplayer tag first. This leaves us with a quite unfortunate choice between:
[list][*] having a Singleplayer tag only
[*] having Local Co-op and Multiplayer tags[/list]
None of this really fits. We believe having Local co-op tag only would be the best.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35018434/411b47d4b7c3af0b3dd60272cfc6c1bd2df9fec9.gif[/img]

Summing up, we just wanted to share this to let you know that, above all, we want to be honest and transparent with you. 

Wish you all the best!

notes.title: Steam Remote Play Together - FAQ
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35018434/00509a82207bd3c9f309fa9a640458be25169f94.jpg[/img]

[h1][b]Dear Renovators,[/b][/h1][b]Tools Up! was designed as a local multiplayer game and we have always advertised it as such.[/b] The recent news about Steam Remote Play Together feature came as a pleasant surprise and we really hoped it would let you play Tools Up! with your friends and family online.

Sadly, we hear reports about the [b]poor performance of Steam Remote Play Together[/b] in some regions, especially Asia. This is a brand new feature, so there might still be room for improvement. We have already reported it to Steam and hopefully you’ll be able to take full advantage of this feature soon. 

It pains us that there’s not much we can do in regard to this matter. We’re waiting for Steam to work this out on their end. Thank you for your patience while this gets worked out.

Lastly, we have prepared a short FAQ (Frequently Asked Questions) for you, in which we explain how this feature works, how you can improve its performance, and present alternatives to Steam Remote Play Together. You can find it below.

Thank you for playing Tools Up! We wish you lots of fun with the game and hope to stay in touch!

Cheers!
All in! Games & The Knights of Unity

[h1][b]FAQ[/b][/h1][b]Steam Remote Play Together is a brand new feature allowing people to play together online. Please refer to [url=https://store.steampowered.com/remoteplay/]Steam Remote Play overview[/url] and [url=https://support.steampowered.com/kb_article.php?ref=3629-RIAV-1617#networkports]Steam Remote Play Support[/url] for more information in your native language.[/b]

[b]Q: How do I use Steam Remote Play Together?[/b]
A: It’s easy! Just follow the three simple steps:
1. Launch Tools Up!
2. Open your Friends List and right-click to
Invite your friends.
3. They accept the invite in the chat window and... That’s it!
You're playing together.

To access your Friends List, you may need to open Steam Overlay (Shift+Tab by default).

[b]Q: Can you play with two keyboards via Steam Remote Play Together?[/b]
A: You can only play Tools Up! with a single keyboard and multiple controllers (Xbox One, Steam Controller, etc.).
 
[b]Q: How does Steam Remote Play work?[/b]
A: Steam Remote Play allows games to be launched on one computer, while being played from other devices connected to Steam. With Remote Play Together, you can invite your Steam Friends to join your local co-op sessions remotely, without having to own or launch the game themselves.

[b]Q: We’re experiencing poor Steam Remote Play Together performance. What can we do?[/b]
A: Below are a few solutions Valve recommends. Please refer to Steam Remote Play overview and Steam Remote Play Support for more information in your native language.
[list][*] [b]Hardware:[/b]We recommend a minimum of a quad-core CPU for the computer running the game. The client has more modest requirements, but should have a GPU that supports hardware accelerated H264 decoding. Any recent laptop or PC should meet the client requirements.
[*] [b]Network:[/b]
We recommend using a wired network for the best streaming experience. People have had some success with powerline networks and wireless N and AC networks with good signal, though your experience may vary.
[*] [b]Game Settings:[/b]
To improve your streaming experience, you can go into your game settings and lower your resolution and turn off vertical sync.
[*] [b]Steam Settings:[/b]
In the Remote Play settings you can change a number of things that can affect your experience. You can change your preference for speed vs quality, limit the network bandwidth, and adjust the maximum capture resolution.[/list]

[b]Q: What network ports does Steam Remote Play use?[/b]
A: Streaming uses UDP ports 27031 and 27036 and TCP ports 27036 and 27037. Please make sure Steam can listen on these ports in your firewall software.

[b]Q: Should I update video drivers?[/b]
A: A number of bugs have been fixed in the latest video driver releases that may affect streaming. If you are getting poor performance, graphical glitches or black screens please make sure you have the latest drivers installed from your video card vendor's website.

[b]Q: What are alternatives to Steam Remote Play Together?[/b]
A: Members of the Tools Up! community have recommended using Parsec, a third-party software, which lets you invite your friends to play games with you online even if the game doesn't have online multiplayer. We don’t officially support this solution, but we hear reports that its performance can be better than Steam Remote Play Together

notes.title: DIY has never been so jolly!
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35018434/e2d480ea05e2f27775e38b7262765f073a5e5a66.gif[/img]

Regular home renovations are hard enough, but have you ever tried painting walls surrounded by lava or carrying a sofa on a slippery floor of ice? You need to watch a lot more than just your step in this crazy world!!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35018434/53aff9b66b82b404e2031ef4167c182d507f59ab.gif[/img]

In Tools Up! it won’t take long to see that this is no ordinary DIY job. You’ll have to deal with a few, um, complications that will make your tasks just a little harder (and funnier!):
[list]
[*] [b]Lava[/b] - A new house design trend, apparently. Keeps your apartment warm during winter and makes it really easy to light your BBQ in the summer.
[*] [b]Water[/b] - The sound of a waterfall is nice and relaxing, which is good since you’ll need to relax after watching your tools get washed away.
[*] [b]Ice[/b] - It’s hard to keep your cool when you’re walking on ice. On the other hand, it’s really easy to fall down. 
[/list]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35018434/6f7021465ae9bfdefaee740629e743e423d5e2de.gif[/img]

notes.title: Tools Up looks like the Overcooked of house renovation
notes.content:
Put that putty knife down, you storming degenerate. You re a terrible decorator, we all know that. But listen, that doesn t mean you can t follow your dream in the fantastical realm of the videogame. Tools Up will let you to indulge in that wallpaper-stripping you love so much. It s a couch co-op game about renovating apartments in a mysterious skyscraper. Four players, a new sofa, some carpets, and plenty of paint. Surely you will fare better at this pretend decorating than you do with all that spackling paste in your bathroom. Surely.
